hints: Evaluate at $x = 2$ to find gradient $-2 \implies$ normal gradient $\frac{1}{2}$.
Form normal equation through $(2, 3)$ to show $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -2(x - 1)^{-3} = -\frac{2}{(x - 1)^3}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal line passing through $A(2, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 2) \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x - 1 + 3 \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2$$

ai_rubric.Normals to Curves: Differentiates to $-2(x-1)^{-3}$ (B1). Finds normal gradient $1/2$ (M1). Shows $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2$ (A1).

walkthrough:
Split the region of revolution into two parts at $x = 2$:
- From $x = 1$ to $x = 2$, bounded by the line $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2$.
- From $x = 2$ to $x = 3$, bounded by the curve $y = (x - 1)^{-2} + 2$.

Integrate the volume under the line from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$:
$$V_1 = \pi \int_1^2 \left(\frac{1}{2}x + 2\right)^2 dx = \pi \left[ \frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}x + 2\right)^3}{3 \times \frac{1}{2}} \right]_1^2 = \frac{2\pi}{3} \left[ 3^3 - 2.5^3 \right] = \frac{2\pi}{3}(27 - 15.625) = \frac{91\pi}{12} = 7\frac{7}{12}\pi$$

Integrate the volume under the curve from $x = 2$ to $x = 3$:
$$y^2 = \left((x - 1)^{-2} + 2\right)^2 = (x - 1)^{-4} + 4(x - 1)^{-2} + 4$$
$$V_2 = \pi \int_2^3 \left((x - 1)^{-4} + 4(x - 1)^{-2} + 4\right) dx = \pi \left[ -\frac{1}{3}(x - 1)^{-3} - 4(x - 1)^{-1} + 4x \right]_2^3$$
$$V_2 = \pi \left( \left(-\frac{1}{24} - 2 + 12\right) - \left(-\frac{1}{3} - 4 + 8\right) \right) = \pi \left( \frac{239}{24} - \frac{11}{3} \right) = \frac{151\pi}{24} = 6\frac{7}{24}\pi$$

Sum the two volumes to determine the total volume of revolution:
$$V = V_1 + V_2 = \frac{91\pi}{12} + \frac{151\pi}{24} = \frac{182\pi + 151\pi}{24} = \frac{333\pi}{24} = \frac{111\pi}{8} = 13\frac{7}{8}\pi \quad (\approx 43.6)$$

ai_rubric.Volumes of Revolution: Integrates line squared (A1, A1). Integrates curve squared (A1, A1). Applies limits (DM1). Adds volumes (DM1). Obtains exact volume $\frac{111\pi}{8}$ (A1).
